easy.def: A small bit of food between meals.
examples: I eat a snack after school.
The snack is an apple.
We packed a snack.

more.def: A small amount of food that you eat between meals.
examples: I eat an apple for a snack after school.
We packed snacks for the long car ride.
The kids shared a snack at recess.

easy.def: A small, unexpected problem.
examples: We hit a snag.
The trip had a snag.
A snag in the plan.

more.def: A small, unexpected problem or obstacle.
examples: We hit a snag when the bus broke down.
The plan had a snag.
The only snag was that it started to rain.

easy.def: To catch on something sharp.
examples: My coat snagged on a nail.
She snagged her sock.
The branch snagged his shirt.

more.def: To catch or tear something on a rough or pointed thing.
examples: My sweater snagged on a nail.
She snagged her sock on a splinter.
The branch snagged his shirt as he walked by.

easy.def: A small animal that moves very slowly and has a shell on its back.
examples: A snail crawled on the leaf.
The snail is slow.
I saw a snail in the garden.

more.def: A small, soft animal with a spiral shell on its back that moves very slowly and leaves a slimy trail.
examples: A snail crawled slowly across the garden path.
The snail pulled its body into its shell when I touched it.
A trail of slime showed where the snail had been.

easy.def: A long animal with no legs that slides on the ground.
examples: The snake slid away.
A snake has scales.
I saw a snake.

more.def: A long, thin animal with no legs and scaly skin.
examples: The snake slid through the grass.
A snake sheds its skin as it grows.
Some snakes live in trees.

easy.def: To break with a sharp sound.
examples: The twig will snap.
The branch snapped in half.
I heard the stick snap.

more.def: To break suddenly with a short, sharp sound.
examples: The dry stick snapped under his foot.
The rubber band snapped when I stretched it too far.
Ice on the pond snapped and cracked.

easy.def: A short, sharp sound.
examples: I heard a snap.
The snap of the twig made me jump.
The lid closed with a snap.

more.def: A sudden, short, sharp sound like something breaking or closing.
examples: The lid shut with a loud snap.
We heard the snap of a branch in the forest.
A snap of her fingers made the dog sit.

easy.def: Quick and lively.
examples: She has a snappy walk.
The song is snappy.
He gave a snappy answer.

more.def: Quick, lively and neat, or stylish and smart.
examples: The marching band played a snappy tune as it came down the street.
He gave a snappy salute and smiled.
She wore a snappy red jacket to the party.

easy.def: To grab quickly.
examples: The bird snatched a crumb.
He snatched the ball.
She snatched her hat.

more.def: To grab something quickly and suddenly.
examples: The seagull snatched a chip from my hand.
He snatched the ball out of the air.
She snatched her hat before the wind took it.

easy.def: To move quietly so no one sees you.
examples: The cat sneaks up.
She sneaked into the room.
He snuck out.

more.def: To move quietly so that no one notices you.
examples: The cat sneaked up on the bird.
She sneaked into the room to surprise her mom.
He sneaked a cookie from the jar.

easy.def: A soft shoe for sports.
examples: I wear sneakers.
The sneaker is white.
My sneakers are muddy.

more.def: A comfortable shoe with a rubber bottom, worn for sports and play.
examples: I tied my sneakers before the race.
One sneaker came untied.
Her sneakers squeaked on the gym floor.

easy.def: Doing things quietly so no one sees.
examples: The cat is sneaky.
He made a sneaky move.
A sneaky fox is in the story.

more.def: Acting in a quiet, secret way, often to do something you should not.
examples: The sneaky cat crept up to the sleeping bird.
She gave her brother a sneaky look and took the last cookie.
A sneaky fox is the villain in the old folk tale.

easy.def: To blow air out of your nose suddenly.
examples: I sneeze when I have a cold.
The dust made me sneeze.
She sneezed.

more.def: To blow air out of your nose and mouth suddenly and loudly.
examples: A loud sneeze echoed through the library.
She sneezed three times in a row.
Cover your mouth when you sneeze.

easy.def: To breathe in through your nose with a short sound.
examples: The dog sniffs the grass.
I sniffed the flower.
She sniffed the soup.

more.def: To breathe in air through your nose in short breaths, to smell something.
examples: The dog sniffed around the yard.
The dog sniffed every bush along the path.
He sniffed because his nose was runny.

easy.def: To cut with small, quick cuts.
examples: I snipped the string.
She snips the paper.
Mom snipped the thread.

more.def: To cut something with a quick, small cut of scissors.
examples: I snipped the string with my scissors.
She snipped a few flowers from the garden.
Dad snipped the tag off my new shirt.

easy.def: A person who thinks they are better than others.
examples: Do not be a snob.
The snob would not play with us.
A snob looks down on others.

more.def: A person who thinks they are better than other people because of their money, clothes or other things.
examples: It is unkind to be a snob and look down on people who have less.
The snob refused to talk to anyone who wore plain clothes.
A good friend is never a snob.

easy.def: To look around where you should not.
examples: Do not snoop.
He snooped in my room.
She snooped around.

more.def: To look around secretly to find out things that are not your business.
examples: Do not snoop in other people's drawers.
He snooped around my room.
The cat snooped in the cupboards.

easy.def: To breathe loudly while you sleep.
examples: Dad snores.
The dog snored.
I heard him snore.

more.def: To make a rough, noisy sound as you breathe while you sleep.
examples: Dad snores loudly at night.
The dog snored on the rug.
I could hear him snore through the wall.

easy.def: To make a loud sound through your nose.
examples: The pig snorted.
The horse snorts.
He snorted with laughter.

more.def: To breathe out noisily through the nose, often to show an animal's feeling or a laugh.
examples: The pig snorted in the mud.
The horse snorted and tossed its head.
He snorted with laughter at the joke.

easy.def: A loud sound through the nose.
examples: The pig let out a snort.
I heard a snort.
He gave a snort.

more.def: A loud, rough sound made by breathing out through the nose.
examples: The pig let out a loud snort.
I heard a snort from the next stall.
He gave a snort of laughter.

easy.def: White flakes of frozen water.
examples: The snow is cold.
We play in the snow.
Snow covered the yard.

more.def: Soft white flakes of frozen water that fall from the sky.
examples: Snow covered the ground overnight.
We built a snowman in the deep snow.
The children caught snow on their tongues.

easy.def: To fall as white flakes.
examples: It snows in winter.
It snowed all night.
I hope it snows.

more.def: To fall from the sky as flakes of ice.
examples: It snows a lot in the mountains.
It snowed for three days.
I hope it snows on my birthday.
